title: Apollo Changelog: April 24, 2023
body_markdown:
## Live GraphQL performance troubleshooting


This week we’re hosting a two-part livestream investigating real-world performance issues in a GraphQL API. Follow along as Michael Watson explores performance issues on[Wednesday, April 26, at 1:30 pm PDT](https://discord.gg/NEPmWUdKn7?event=1098661954253492224) . Then, on[Thursday at 11:00 am PDT](https://discord.gg/NEPmWUdKn7?event=1098662301407654000) , we’ll solve those performance problems by implementing server-side caching! You can catch all of our livestreams in[our Discord server](https://discord.gg/NEPmWUdKn7) .


## Announcing Summit sessions


As talks are confirmed for GraphQL Summit 2023, we’re updating the[list of sessions](https://summit.graphql.com/event/c51538f6-4b76-44e3-871e-54180c77cad8/websitePage:aa37bf00-dba5-4e19-912a-01aad46f7426) with details. Right now, we have topics covering:


- GraphQL security
- Best practices for Federation
- Migration stories from monoliths to supergraphs
- Designing UIs using GraphQL data
- Schema design
- Leveraging GraphQL directives


Keep an eye on the Summit site for more talk announcements!


## Rapid roundup


- [Apollo Server 4.7.0 allows opting out of embedded Sandbox telemetry](https://github.com/apollographql/apollo-server/releases/tag/%40apollo%2Fserver%404.7.0)
- [Apollo Kotlin 3.8.1 is out with two bug fixes](https://github.com/apollographql/apollo-kotlin/releases/tag/v3.8.1)
- [Rover 0.14.0](https://github.com/apollographql/rover/releases/tag/v0.14.0) supports custom introspection headers during composition and URL validation during subgraph publishes, along with several bug fixes and improvements.
- [Apollo Router 1.15.1](https://github.com/apollographql/router/releases/tag/v1.15.1) comes with JWT algorithm restrictions, improvements to Helm charts, a fix to Docker builds, and many more improvements
- [Tech note: Federation is not a saga orchestrator](https://www.apollographql.com/docs/technotes/TN0040-federation-is-not-a-saga-orchestrator/)


## Community spotlight


We want to give a special shoutout to Ari and Lloyd on[our Discord server](https://discord.gg/NEPmWUdKn7) . They’ve been sharing the details of their journeys with Apollo Federation and GraphOS—details that are helping us improve our products and documentation! If *you* have any questions, comments, suggestions, or complaints about anything under the Apollo sun, be like Ari and Lloyd and let us know.


Written by


Dylan Anthony
